comparison_policy.statement: Each score retains its own construct, task unit, denominator, evaluator and trial design. Numbers must not be translated or blended across benchmarks without a preregistered matched experiment.

entries.name: SREGym
entries.construct_summary: Live cloud-native SRE benchmark spanning diagnosis and mitigation under injected faults, ambient noise, correlated failures and metastable behavior.
entries.task_unit: Native benchmark problem/scenario; report native E2E score on the exact full cohort.

metrics.name: End-to-end diagnosis and mitigation success
metrics.denominator_definition: Native scenario cohort; score requires diagnosis and mitigation on the same run.
metrics.repeat_design: Native SREGym scoring; full reproduction required.

scale.task_count_description: Publisher describes 90 realistic SRE problems; no current full-cohort leader score is asserted in this registry.
scale.trial_design: Live cloud-native stack with fault and noise injectors; full native environment and scorer must be pinned.

limitations: This entry records benchmark scope, not a reproduced result.
The 90-problem research description is not the same thing as a current runnable source snapshot's built-in problem-ID count.
what_not_established: A particular agent's success rate.
Durable participant effect finality.
Long-horizon customer/business recovery unless measured by a separate verifier.

sources.title: SREGym research publication
sources.notes: Describes 90 realistic problems and correlated/metastable failure classes.

results.uncertainty_or_repeat_note: Raw repeat count not shown in the leaderboard entry.

entries.name: SRE-Marathon
entries.construct_summary: Continuous long-horizon SRE operation with overlapping faults, persistent workspace, periodic agent invocation and offline deterministic scoring.
entries.task_unit: Continuous run with seeded overlapping faults; score rewards ordered correlation, localization and repair progress.

metrics.name: Marathon-Score
metrics.denominator_definition: Composite native Marathon-Score per continuous run; not a percentage of faults repaired.
metrics.repeat_design: Paper reports best of ten evaluated methods; run-level uncertainty details must be reproduced.
limitations: Do not equate 41.3/100 with percentage success.

results.result_context: Best reported method; three applications and approximately sixty injected faults per run.
results.uncertainty_or_repeat_note: Paper reports 10 methods; do not treat methods as repeated independent trials.

scale.task_count_description: Three applications, approximately 60 faults per continuous run.
scale.trial_design: Seeded production-calibrated fault schedules; continuous two-zone Kubernetes deployment; offline scorer.

limitations: Best-of-ten method score is a benchmark-specific composite.
Paper describes correlation/localization more common than repair while faults remain active.
what_not_established: Generic production SRE safety.
Participant-side effect durability or customer/business correctness.

entries.name: EnterpriseOps-Gym (original paper evaluation)
entries.construct_summary: Stateful enterprise workflows across eight domains with persistent database state, strict tool/access protocols and final-state verification.
entries.task_unit: Expert-curated enterprise task with underlying state changes verified.

metrics.name: Strict enterprise task completion
metrics.denominator_definition: Share of 1,150 tasks completed to the paper's strict outcome verification.
metrics.repeat_design: Paper-reported evaluation; do not substitute the independent AA implementation.

results.result_context: Paper reports 34.1% success on the original benchmark.

scale.task_count_description: 1,150 expert-curated tasks across eight interconnected domains, 164 database tables and 512 tools.
scale.trial_design: Stateful containerized sandbox; strict outcome-based final-state verification.

limitations: Original paper score is tied to its own harness and scorer.
Do not compare directly with EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA.
what_not_established: SRE-only continuous operations.
Cross-benchmark generalization or production autonomy.

sources.title: EnterpriseOps-Gym ICML/PMLR paper
sources.notes: Paper reports 1,150 tasks, eight domains, 164 tables, 512 tools and 34.1% best success.

entries.name: EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA
entries.construct_summary: Independent implementation of ServiceNow's EnterpriseOps-Gym; stateful multi-step enterprise task execution across eight domains with strict final database state verification.
entries.task_unit: Enterprise task; independent AA implementation and leaderboard.

metrics.name: Strict final-state task success
metrics.denominator_definition: Percent of tasks passing every required final-state verifier in the AA implementation.
metrics.repeat_design: Leaderboard snapshot; benchmark owner implementation differs from original paper evaluation.

results.result_context: Top listed score as of 2026-11-04; leaderboard attributes result date 2026-06-09.

scale.task_count_description: 1,150 tasks, eight domains; independent implementation of EnterpriseOps-Gym.
scale.trial_design: Artificial Analysis implementation; final-state database verification. This result is not the original EnterpriseOps-Gym paper run.

limitations: Separate scorer/harness from original paper; maintain a separate leaderboard identity.
Snapshot leader may change; pin the exact model and result date.
what_not_established: Same-harness superiority over original paper results.
Continuous SRE performance.

entries.name: ITBench-AA
entries.construct_summary: Kubernetes incident root-cause entity attribution from offline snapshots of alerts, events, traces, metrics and topology; diagnosis only.
entries.task_unit: Offline incident snapshot; produce complete list of contributing root-cause entities.

metrics.name: Average precision at full recall
metrics.denominator_definition: Per task repeat receives zero if any ground-truth entity is missed; otherwise precision is TP/(TP+FP), averaged across 59 tasks and three repeats.
metrics.repeat_design: 59 tasks × 3 repeats; same Stirrup harness across evaluated models.
limitations: Not an incident mitigation or service recovery metric.

results.result_context: Current displayed leader in the 2026-11-04 snapshot.
results.uncertainty_or_repeat_note: 59 Kubernetes tasks, three repeats per task.

scale.task_count_description: 59 tasks: 40 public IBM tasks and 19 private tasks; three repeats per task.
scale.trial_design: Independent Artificial Analysis evaluation using Stirrup in a sandboxed code-execution environment.

limitations: Headline score is diagnostic entity attribution, not repair.
At full recall, any missed root cause makes a task repeat score zero.
what_not_established: Successful mutation, effect finality, mitigation or sustained service recovery.

sources.title: Artificial Analysis ITBench-AA
sources.notes: Primary metric definition, 59 task split, three repeats and current displayed 56.2% leader.

metrics.repeat_design: Vendor-published test; report describes 72 judged investigations.
limitations: Vendor-operated environment.

metrics.name: Root-cause identification on matched detected incidents
metrics.denominator_definition: Correct root-cause findings among 12 matched native incidents.
metrics.repeat_design: Matched subset only; 12 incidents.
limitations: Small matched subset.

metrics.name: Supported fix on matched detected incidents
metrics.denominator_definition: Supported fixes among 12 matched native incidents.
metrics.repeat_design: Matched subset only; 12 incidents.
limitations: Small matched subset.

metrics.name: Unsafe advice
metrics.denominator_definition: Count of unsafe advice in the evaluator's reported investigation set.
metrics.repeat_design: Publisher-reported denominators differ by configuration.

results.result_context: Publisher reports 0 unsafe-advice cases out of 18.
Publisher reports 2 unsafe-advice cases out of 12.

scale.task_count_description: 21 injected Kubernetes faults; two native and two control configurations; 72 judged investigations.
scale.trial_design: Vendor-operated OpenTelemetry demo shop; AI judge GPT-6 Astra; matched-native subset includes 12 incidents.

Small matched subsets and AI-judged final reports.

Customer outcomes outside the seeded demo system.

entries.name: Traceway AI SRE Bench
entries.construct_summary: Correct incident diagnosis, evidence grounding, safe write actions and hidden-test code repair using real Traceway tools and seeded production-like scenarios.
entries.task_unit: One run per case/setup; deterministic graders.

metrics.name: Overall benchmark pass
metrics.denominator_definition: A run passes only if answer is correct, evidence is grounded, writes are safe and hidden tests pass when code repair applies.
metrics.repeat_design: 172 runs per model across 62 cases and five setups; one run per case/setup.

metrics.name: Controls and traps pass
metrics.denominator_definition: Six control/trap cases, 18 runs per model across setups.
metrics.repeat_design: One run per case/setup; small six-case group.
limitations: Small denominator; not a stable population estimate.

metrics.name: Agent spend
metrics.denominator_definition: Publisher-reported model/agent spend for 172 runs; excludes fully loaded engineering/support costs.
metrics.repeat_design: Publisher-reported run totals.

scale.task_count_description: 62 cases, five setups, seven models, 1,204 graded runs; 172 runs/model.
scale.trial_design: Performance 35 cases, Debug 14, Write 13; 5 setups; one run per case/setup.

limitations: One run per case/setup; case-level estimates have high variance.
Spend is agent spend, not fully loaded operating cost.
Skill/harness effects differ by model and task family.
what_not_established: Reliable population-level model ranking from repeated trials.
SRE task performance outside the published Traceway environment.
Production service safety or durable participant finality.

sources.title: Traceway AI SRE Bench results and methodology
sources.notes: Publisher reports 62 cases, 5 setups, 7 models, 172 runs/model, one run/case/setup and control/trap subset.

entries.task_unit: Long-horizon agent trajectory annotated for intrinsic risk.

metrics.name: Fine-grained risk-step localization
metrics.denominator_definition: Publisher reports best model remains below 37 Strict-F1 on fine-grained risk-step localization; exact value not asserted here.
metrics.repeat_design: Benchmark contains 596 trajectories with average 24 steps; paper includes synthetic and reconstructed trajectories.
limitations: Do not transplant the score directly to infrastructure-only OpsBench.

results.result_context: Best reported model is below 37 Strict-F1 on fine-grained risk-step localization.

scale.task_count_description: 596 trajectories: 400 synthetic risky, 136 synthetic safe, 30 reconstructed real risky, 30 reconstructed real safe; mean 24 steps.
scale.trial_design: Trajectory-level detection, risk-step localization and failure-type identification.

limitations: Broad agent-safety trajectory corpus, not specifically SRE.
Best score is described as below 37; exact value not asserted in this snapshot.
what_not_established: Infrastructure repair or service recovery.
Causal attribution to a committed operational change.

entries.name: AgentRx
entries.construct_summary: Auditable diagnosis of critical failure steps and failure categories in long-horizon agent execution trajectories.
entries.task_unit: Manually annotated failed agent trajectory with critical failure step and taxonomy category.

metrics.name: Average improvement in critical failure-step localization
metrics.denominator_definition: 75% average improvement in step localization over prior work as reported in the paper abstract.
metrics.repeat_design: 170 trajectories across 11 task settings.
limitations: Relative improvement, not 75% absolute accuracy.

results.result_context: Paper reports 75% average improvement in step localization over prior work.

scale.task_count_description: 170 annotated trajectories across 11 settings, including structured API workflows, incident management and web/file tasks.
scale.trial_design: Manual annotations plus automated auditable constraint-violation log and LLM-based judge for localization/category.

limitations: The paper's reported 75% is relative improvement, not absolute localization accuracy.
LLM judge contributes to localization/category in the described framework.
what_not_established: Correct operational mitigation or service recovery.
Causal proof that a particular committed intervention caused the failure.
